html:
AI search visibility — we'll map out where to start, 1:1Get an SEO/GEO audit
    • Customers
    • Pricing
    Go to Dashboard
    Analysis & Diagnosis

    Competitor AI Gap Analysis

    A 7-day playbook to find your 'real competitors' in AI answers and reclaim source share

    5–7 days|Intermediate|PR/Content/SEO/Brand Team
    Start Free AnalysisSee all workflows

    Contents

    When you hear 'our name doesn't appear in AI search,' the more accurate diagnosis is this — it's not that your name isn't appearing, but that someone else is taking your spot. That 'someone else' might not be a direct competitor. News outlets, comparison platforms, and public institutions are often the bigger issue.

    What you'll get

    AI answer market competition map (direct + source competitors)
    SEO×GEO integrated gap matrix
    Platform-specific (ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/Perplexity) weakness report
    Competitive content reverse-engineering report
    Source graph attack plan
    30/90-day execution backlog

    Success Metrics

    GEO Share of Voice+5%p (30d) / +15%p (90d)
    Citation Rate2× (30d) / 3× (90d)
    Competitor-overtaken questions/keywords+20% (30d) / +50% (90d)

    Step-by-step guide

    • Check top 10 domains in GEO Insights → Visibility Leaderboard (last 28 days)
    • List 3-5 direct competitors
    • List 5-10 source competitors (news, institutions, comparison platforms, communities)
    • Write 1-page domain share summary

    Pro Tip

    When your share is low and 'Others' is high, many teams think 'we need more content,' but the real reason is usually a source structure problem. Separate the causes first.
    • Classify keywords by gap type — only us strong / both strong / both absent / only competitor strong
    • Select 5-10 Quick Win candidates

    Strategy by Gap Type

    TypeMeaningAction Now
    Only us strongMaintain existing strengthKeep freshness and structure
    Both strongIntense competitionDifferentiate with depth/trust/freshness
    Both absentPreemption opportunityBuild reference hub first
    Only competitor strongRecapture priority targetTop priority for quick improvement

    Pro Tip

    Brand head keywords are hard to overturn with content alone since news/portals are strong. But procedure/condition keywords like 'claim documents' can be quickly reversed with reference hubs.
    • Compose Top 20 questions (10 recommendation/comparison + 10 procedure/caution)
    • Create mapping table of 'who's winning now' per question

    How to Interpret Question Gaps

    • •We're mentioned but not cited → document structure issue (no answers, FAQs, tables)
    • •Competitors are cited but we're not → trust structure issue (weak source evidence)
    • •Only news/institutions are cited → source graph issue (our domain isn't linked as reference)
    • Derive 'our weakest questions Top 5' per platform
    • Create improvement checklist per platform

    Platform-Specific Attack Points

    • •ChatGPT — Prefers well-organized documents with clear definitions, summaries, FAQs. One-sentence definition in first paragraph is essential
    • •Claude — Values balance, accuracy, source clarity. Strengthen exceptions, caveats, evidence links
    • •Gemini — Heavily influenced by SEO signals. Maintain structured data + rankings + freshness
    • •Perplexity — Update logs (dates, versions) and reference links are key
    • Write 1-page 'why they win' summary per competitor
    • Finalize reference hub template we need to create

    6 Things to Check

    • •Content format — guide, comparison, checklist, FAQ, or tutorial
    • •Document structure — answer-first in first paragraph, includes tables/lists/FAQs
    • •Evidence structure — public institution citations, numbers, definitions, exception notices
    • •Freshness — presence of update dates and change history
    • •Internal links — hub-cluster structure
    • •Structured data — FAQPage/Article schema applied

    Pro Tip

    News outlets capture AI sources not because they're 'news,' but because information is accumulated in the most organized form. If we build that form, we can reverse the situation.
    • Create source graph target list
    • Prioritize '10 channels to connect per reference hub'
    • Fix 1 reference URL in [References] for URL-possible channels
    • Standardize and repeat exact page titles for URL-difficult channels
    • 40%+ — Defense mode (maintain freshness and trust structure)
    • 20-40% — Pursuit mode (overtake with depth and accuracy)
    • 10-20% — Focus mode (win only in specific question clusters)
    • Below 10% — Preemption mode (build reference hubs on empty topics first)

    30/90-Day Execution Backlog Structure

    • •30 days: 10 Quick Wins (SEO-strong/AI-weak areas + citation-inducing procedure questions)
    • •90 days: Expand 5 reference hubs + systematize source graph

    Common questions

    Data collection takes one day; including strategy building, it takes 5-7 days.

    Check top domains in GEO Insights → Visibility Leaderboard (last 28 days) to immediately spot unexpected source competitors.

    Quick Wins (adding FAQs, applying schema) show changes within 2-4 weeks. Reference hub construction takes 1-3 months.

Step-by-step guide
Day 1
Build the Competitor Map

You need to view competitors in two categories: direct competitors sell the same products/services, while SERP/source competitors don't sell your product but keep getting cited by AI as sources.

Check top 10 domains in GEO Insights → Visibility Leaderboard (last 28 days)
List 3-5 direct competitors
List 5-10 source competitors (news, institutions, comparison platforms, communities)
Write 1-page domain share summary

Pro Tip

When your share is low and 'Others' is high, many teams think 'we need more content,' but the real reason is usually a source structure problem. Separate the causes first.
Day 2
SEO Keyword Gap Analysis

AI answers and search don't move independently. Gemini heavily reflects Google SEO signals, so HaloX views both together.

Classify keywords by gap type — only us strong / both strong / both absent / only competitor strong
Select 5-10 Quick Win candidates
Strategy by Gap Type
Type	Meaning	Action Now
Only us strong	Maintain existing strength	Keep freshness and structure
Both strong	Intense competition	Differentiate with depth/trust/freshness
Both absent	Preemption opportunity	Build reference hub first
Only competitor strong	Recapture priority target	Top priority for quick improvement

Pro Tip

Brand head keywords are hard to overturn with content alone since news/portals are strong. But procedure/condition keywords like 'claim documents' can be quickly reversed with reference hubs.
Day 3
GEO Question Gap Analysis

Even for the same question, the source changes depending on which domain answers. Run question sets in HaloX and compare 'who dominates AI answers.'

Compose Top 20 questions (10 recommendation/comparison + 10 procedure/caution)
Create mapping table of 'who's winning now' per question
How to Interpret Question Gaps
•
We're mentioned but not cited → document structure issue (no answers, FAQs, tables)
•
Competitors are cited but we're not → trust structure issue (weak source evidence)
•
Only news/institutions are cited → source graph issue (our domain isn't linked as reference)
Day 4
Understand Platform Differences

ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity choose different sources for the same question.

Derive 'our weakest questions Top 5' per platform
Create improvement checklist per platform
Platform-Specific Attack Points
•
ChatGPT — Prefers well-organized documents with clear definitions, summaries, FAQs. One-sentence definition in first paragraph is essential
•
Claude — Values balance, accuracy, source clarity. Strengthen exceptions, caveats, evidence links
•
Gemini — Heavily influenced by SEO signals. Maintain structured data + rankings + freshness
•
Perplexity — Update logs (dates, versions) and reference links are key
Day 5
Reverse-Engineer Competitive Content

Analyze specifically why they get cited.

Write 1-page 'why they win' summary per competitor
Finalize reference hub template we need to create
6 Things to Check
•
Content format — guide, comparison, checklist, FAQ, or tutorial
•
Document structure — answer-first in first paragraph, includes tables/lists/FAQs
•
Evidence structure — public institution citations, numbers, definitions, exception notices
•
Freshness — presence of update dates and change history
•
Internal links — hub-cluster structure
•
Structured data — FAQPage/Article schema applied

Pro Tip

News outlets capture AI sources not because they're 'news,' but because information is accumulated in the most organized form. If we build that form, we can reverse the situation.
Day 6
Source Graph Attack Plan

For your domain to enter AI's frequently cited source pool, external domains must link to your references.

Create source graph target list
Prioritize '10 channels to connect per reference hub'
Fix 1 reference URL in [References] for URL-possible channels
Standardize and repeat exact page titles for URL-difficult channels
Day 7
Confirm Strategic Position & Execution Backlog

Your operational mode differs based on current share position.

40%+ — Defense mode (maintain freshness and trust structure)
20-40% — Pursuit mode (overtake with depth and accuracy)
10-20% — Focus mode (win only in specific question clusters)
Below 10% — Preemption mode (build reference hubs on empty topics first)
30/90-Day Execution Backlog Structure
•
30 days: 10 Quick Wins (SEO-strong/AI-weak areas + citation-inducing procedure questions)
•
90 days: Expand 5 reference hubs + systematize source graph
